statement: In South Carolina you petition a family court judge for a name change, and you must have been a resident of South Carolina for at least six months.
detail: You must attach to your petition a SLED fingerprint and criminal background check, a Department of Social Services screening statement covering the Central Registry of Child Abuse and Neglect, a SLED sex-offender-registry screening statement, and a signed affidavit about any child-support or alimony order. The court may waive the six-month residency requirement for a petitioner who is a victim of domestic violence, stalking, or similar abuse and who is currently in reasonable fear for their safety.

cost.note: The filing fee is set by a separate statute and isn't a dollar amount stated here; the SLED background check carries its own separate fee too. Contact the family court clerk for current amounts.

source.title: South Carolina Code of Laws — Title 15, Chapter 49, Change of Name

topic: South Carolina Family Court filing fee for a name change
statement: The South Carolina Judicial Branch's Family Court filing-fee schedule lists a $150 filing fee for Name Change and Correction of Birth Record Actions.
detail: The same schedule says no filing fee is required for a case filed with an order granting a Motion for Leave to Proceed in Forma Pauperis (Rule 3(b)(1), SCRCP). It also lists no fee when a party is represented by an attorney working on behalf of a legal aid society, a legal services or other nonprofit organization, or the South Carolina Pro Bono Program, with written certification from the attorney (Rule 3(b)(2), SCRCP). Motion fees are listed separately. Check the court's own fee page for the current amount before you file.

cost.note: The filing fee for Name Change and Correction of Birth Record Actions. The schedule lists no fee for a case filed with an order granting a Motion for Leave to Proceed in Forma Pauperis.

source.title: South Carolina Judicial Branch — Family Court Filing Fees

topic: South Carolina driver's license and ID name change
statement: To change the name on your South Carolina driver's license or ID card, you complete an Application for Name and/or Address Change (Form 4057) and an Application for a Beginner's Permit, Driver's License, or Identification Card (Form 447-NC), then present documentation such as a marriage license, divorce decree, or a court order issued by your county's family court.
detail: You must update your name with the Social Security Administration at least 48 hours before visiting the SCDMV. A new license reflecting your updated name costs $10, or $25 if you're getting your first REAL ID at the same time. You only have one opportunity to change your name when you marry — changing to a different variation of your married name later takes a court order.

cost.note: This is the standard fee for a new license reflecting a name change. Your first REAL ID is $25 instead, since it's treated as a license renewal.

source.title: South Carolina DMV — Change My Address or Name

topic: South Carolina driver's license and ID sex/gender designation
statement: The SCDMV's own instructions for updating your name or address make no mention of changing a sex or gender designation on a license or ID card.
detail: The page describes exactly what to bring for a name change — a marriage license, divorce decree, family-court order, or preferred-name documents — and says nothing about a sex-designation change process. Confirm directly with the SCDMV before assuming a route exists.

source.title: South Carolina DMV — Change My Address or Name

topic: South Carolina birth certificate name change
statement: South Carolina can only change the name on your birth certificate with a certified court order — the Department of Public Health says name changes and adoptions can only be applied to the record that way.
detail: A certified court order carries a raised or inky seal; a photocopy isn't accepted, and the department keeps one certified copy permanently, so get more than one certified copy from the court. Most in-person amendment requests are completed within 1-2 business days, but court-ordered amendments may take up to 2 weeks. There's an additional $15 amendment fee, and a copy issued within the past year can be replaced for $3.

cost.note: This is the additional amendment fee once the court order is processed. A record issued within the past year can be replaced for $3.

timeline.typical: 1 to 2 business days, or up to 2 weeks for court-ordered amendments

source.title: South Carolina Department of Public Health — Birth Certificates

topic: South Carolina birth certificate sex designation
statement: South Carolina's Department of Public Health describes how to correct errors and process court-ordered name changes on a birth certificate, but its public guidance does not describe any process for changing the sex marker based on gender identity.
detail: The page lists what can be fixed with a notarized affidavit (like a misspelled name or wrong date of birth) and what needs a certified court order (name changes and adoptions). Changing the recorded sex isn't mentioned in either category. Confirm current requirements directly with Vital Records before assuming a route exists.

source.title: South Carolina Department of Public Health — Birth Certificates
